kill_argument: check_sas_listing.py was written blind to a listing nobody has seen, so its most likely outcome is not a wrong number but a crash, and the plan has no rule for a crash: design.data prescribes what to do after a mismatch (deviation, new code round, --replace), not after a parse failure, and after this round only one code round (r4) remains. A 1993 listing with ASA carriage-control characters in column 1, or a PROC REG step that did not run, makes the script stop with 'found 1 LWAGE76 models'; fixing that means looking at the outcome listing the design keeps closed. And even a clean 6/6 match proves less than the docstring says: it covers only the two OLS log-wage regressions of read1.sas, not nearc4, age76/age762 or anything in Panel B or the 2SLS SE formula. I attacked the code and it held: model identification by dependent variable plus parameter count (16/30 from read1.sas), N as Observations Used or C Total df + 1 cross-checked against the error df, the H1 rounding rule at printed decimals, in-memory read with no text printed, continuation pages, SAS 6 and SAS 9 layouts, and loud failure when blocks merge or rows are missed (my own synthetic listings). The fig_chr.py edit changes only the plotting, and the figure metrics are identical to those already recorded.

findings.text: The script's failure paths (CheckFailed when the listing does not hold exactly two LWAGE76 models with 16 and 30 parsed parameters, no ED76 row, no N, or error df != N - k) are all loud, which is right, but no rule says what happens after a non-zero exit. design.data plans only the mismatch path. A parse failure is plausible for a listing nobody has opened: in my synthetic test, a single ASA carriage-control character in column 1 ('0' or '1', common in mainframe-era .lst files) makes the parser find 1 LWAGE76 model and stop; a 'proc reg s' that SAS rejected would leave no PROC REG output at all. A fix would need someone to look at the listing's layout, and after code-r3 only code round 4 remains. Remedy (no code change now): before the run, the PI records in runs/NOTES.md or design.deviations that a failed run stays in the ledger; that the Econometrician may then look at the listing's line layout only (all claims are already frozen, so this cannot tune a claim); that the parser fix is a recorded deviation reviewed in code-r4; and that if the code-r4 version also fails, the check is reported as not completed rather than run with --unreviewed.

findings.text: The docstring (and threat T3) overstate what a match can show. The two read1.sas log-wage models contain ed76, exp76, exp762, black, smsa76r, reg76r, smsa66r, reg662-reg669 and the family-background block. A 6/6 match therefore confirms the OLS of Table 2 columns 2 and 5 on this file, including the sample, but not nearc4, age76/age762, the Panel A/B 2SLS columns, or the B1-B4 misses. read1.sas also reads 'nls.flt', so T3's 'Card's own program on this file' is what the check tests, not a premise. A mismatch cannot by itself separate the file vintage from a code error. Remedy (narrow the claim): the sas-ols-match claim text names only the two OLS log-wage regressions of read1.sas (Table 2 cols 2 and 5) and N; it does not generalise to 'data reading and variable construction' or to any IV result. All 6 items are counted, with the diffs reported, and no tolerance is loosened after the run.
findings.evidence: code/check_sas_listing.py lines 27-29 (docstring 'confirms the data reading and variable construction'); data/raw/proximity/read1.sas (infile nls.flt; four models under proc reg s); plan.json design.threats T3
findings.response: Fixed in the brief and D5: the claim is narrowed to the two OLS regressions and N, all six comparisons reported with differences, tolerance fixed.
